evals.expected_output: The skill reads issue #42 from zircote/swagger-php, triages it by classifying type/priority/area from the issue content, applies labels, removes triage labels, then routes to the appropriate action workflow based on the classification.
expectations: The skill runs 'gh issue view 42 --repo zircote/swagger-php' with JSON fields including number, title, body, labels, assignees, state, comments to fetch the full issue context
The skill applies a type label (one of type/bug, type/feature, type/docs, type/question, type/chore) based on keyword analysis of the issue title and body
The skill applies a priority label (one of priority/critical, priority/high, priority/medium, priority/low) based on severity indicators in the issue content
The skill removes 'needs-triage' and/or 'status/triage' labels after classification using 'gh issue edit 42 --repo zircote/swagger-php --remove-label'

For a bug or feature issue, the skill creates a branch named 'gh-do/issue-42-<slug>' from the main branch SHA and creates a draft PR whose body starts with 'Resolves zircote/swagger-php#42' on its own line before the Summary section

evals.prompt: hey can you process this bug report? it's issue 15 in my current repo. the user says the login page crashes when they enter special characters
evals.expected_output: The skill detects single-item mode with issue 15, resolves the current repo via gh repo view, triages the issue as type/bug with appropriate priority, and routes to the bug fix workflow.
expectations: The skill resolves the current repo by running 'gh repo view --json nameWithOwner -q .nameWithOwner' since no --repo flag was provided
The skill classifies the issue as 'type/bug' because the prompt mentions 'bug report' and 'crashes'
The skill assigns at least priority/medium (the default for bugs) or higher given the crash keyword
The skill creates a feature branch with the pattern 'gh-do/issue-15-<slug>' and proceeds to implement a fix rather than just triaging
The skill creates a draft PR with 'Resolves <owner>/<repo>#15' in the PR body (not just the title), followed by Summary, Changes, and Test Plan sections

evals.expected_output: The skill assembles a prioritized queue from zircote/swagger-php, reports what would be done for each item without executing mutations, and presents a numbered checklist plan.
expectations: The skill runs the preflight check to verify the 'needs-triage' label exists in zircote/swagger-php, creating it if missing

The skill queries post-triage issues (labeled but NOT needs-triage/status-triage), unlabeled issues as fallback, PRs with changes requested, PRs with failing checks, and discussions — gathering all candidate items that are ready for implementation

The skill orders the queue by the defined priority: critical issues first, then high, then PRs with changes requested, then PRs with failing CI, then medium issues, then discussions, then low issues, then unlabeled issues, then draft PRs
Because --dry-run is set, the skill reports planned labels and actions for each item WITHOUT executing any mutations (no gh issue edit, no gh pr create, no branch creation)
The output is limited to at most 5 items due to --limit 5

evals.expected_output: The skill assembles the queue and, finding more than 1 item, auto-escalates to swarm mode with parallel workers using TeamCreate and TaskCreate.
expectations: The skill assembles the prioritized queue from zircote/swagger-php using the same discovery logic as sweep (post-triage labeled issues, unlabeled issues as fallback, PRs needing attention, discussions)
When the queue contains more than 1 item, the skill reports 'escalating to swarm mode' and does NOT process items sequentially
The skill calls TeamCreate with team_name 'gh-do-swarm' to create the parallel processing team
The skill creates ALL tasks upfront from the queue using TaskCreate (one task per item, up to 8 items from --limit), each with item details including type, repo, number, title, priority, and URL
Each task description includes confirmation rules: draft PRs and labels proceed without asking, but merging PRs and closing issues are flagged for leader review

evals.expected_output: The skill reads PR #33, determines its state (changes requested, approved, draft, or failing CI), triages it, then routes to the correct PR sub-workflow.
expectations: The skill runs 'gh pr view 33 --repo zircote/swagger-php' with JSON fields including reviews, statusCheckRollup, isDraft, mergeable, headRefName, baseRefName, and also fetches the diff with 'gh pr diff 33'
The skill applies a size label based on the file count and diff line count of the PR
For a PR with changes requested: the skill checks out the PR branch, reads review comments, implements requested changes, commits, pushes, and re-requests review — it does NOT create a new PR
For a PR that is approved with passing checks: the skill asks the user for confirmation before merging, it does NOT auto-merge
For a PR with failing checks: the skill reads CI logs, checks out the branch, fixes failures, commits and pushes, then reports what was fixed

evals.expected_output: The skill reads discussion #8 via GraphQL, determines its category, and routes to the correct discussion workflow.
expectations: The skill fetches the discussion using the GraphQL API query that retrieves id, title, body, category name, comments, and labels — not the REST API since discussions are not available via gh issue/pr view

If the discussion category is 'Ideas' or describes a feature request: the skill creates a new issue from the discussion using 'gh issue create' with a link back to the discussion URL, then follows the Issue Workflow to create a branch and draft PR that references the NEW issue number (not the discussion number) with 'Resolves owner/repo#N'
If the discussion category is 'Q&A': the skill drafts an answer based on codebase analysis and posts it as a comment, potentially marking it as answered
If the discussion category is 'RFCs': the skill posts a structured review comment covering feasibility, risks, and alternatives
The skill comments on the discussion linking any newly created issue, so the discussion author is notified of the conversion

evals.expected_output: The skill assembles the queue, creates the swarm team, creates all tasks upfront, spawns 8 parallel workers with worktree isolation, and enters the leader coordination loop.
expectations: The skill creates the team with TeamCreate using team_name 'gh-do-swarm' before spawning any workers

The skill creates ALL tasks upfront from the prioritized queue (up to 20 from --limit) using TaskCreate, each with subject format '[repo] type #N: title' and detailed description including item type, repo, number, priority, and instructions
The skill spawns exactly 8 worker agents (matching --batch 8) as background teammates, each with isolation: 'worktree' to prevent branch collisions between workers

Each worker prompt instructs workers to loop continuously (claim task, execute, complete, claim next) until no pending unowned tasks remain — workers must NOT stop after one task or wait for leader instructions between tasks

The leader monitors progress via SendMessage from workers, handles flags for destructive actions (merge, close) by presenting them to the user for confirmation, and sends shutdown_request when all tasks complete

evals.expected_output: The skill receives only a bare number with no type specified, auto-detects whether #99 is an issue, PR, or discussion, resolves the current repo, and proceeds with the appropriate workflow.
expectations: The skill resolves the repo from 'gh repo view --json nameWithOwner -q .nameWithOwner' since no --repo was provided
The skill auto-detects the item type by trying issue first ('gh issue view 99'), then PR ('gh pr view 99'), then discussion (GraphQL query) — it does NOT require the user to specify the type
After detecting the item type, the skill proceeds through the full triage pipeline: classify type/priority/area, apply labels, remove triage labels
The skill routes to the correct action workflow based on the detected item type (Issue Workflow, PR Workflow, or Discussion Workflow) without asking the user which type it is
If the item cannot be found as any type (issue, PR, or discussion), the skill reports a clear error rather than proceeding with assumptions
